exposure: Gestational weight gain (GWG) categories (low, normal, high)
cohort: The study population comprised 604 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies from Counties Manukau Health, Auckland, New Zealand, representing a multi-ethnic sample with a high prevalence of overweight/obesity and those from high deprivation areas.
finding: The majority of participants (70.7%) had high gestational weight gain, which was associated with increased infant birthweight, while low gestational weight gain was linked to increased odds of Small for Gestational Age (SGA) and Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM).
birth_weight: Babies born to the study participants; birthweight was a measured outcome, showing a linear association with GWG.
